questions.question:
Find the value of the following expression.

sin(30 + θ) - cos(60 - θ)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

sin(30 + theta) - cos(60 - theta)

**Formula used:**

sin(30 + theta) = sin 30 cos theta + cos 30 sin theta

cos(60 - theta) = cos 60 cos theta + sin 60 sin theta

**Calculation:**

sin(30 + theta) - cos(60 - theta)

sin 30 cos theta + cos 30 sin theta - (cos 60 cos theta + sin 60 sin theta)

⇒ (1)/(2) cos theta + frac{sqrt{3}}{2} sin theta - ((1)/(2) cos theta + frac{sqrt{3}}{2} sin theta)

⇒ (1)/(2) cos theta + frac{sqrt{3}}{2} sin theta - (1)/(2) cos theta - frac{sqrt{3}}{2} sin theta

⇒ 0

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: A sells a bike to B at 45% profit. Then B sells it to C at 30% profit. If C pays ₹43,355, then what is the cost price of the bike for A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the **ratio method**: 45% = 9/20 and 30% = 3/10.

Cost Price to Selling Price ratios: (20 → 29) and (10 → 13).

Combined ratio for **A** to **C**: (20 × 10) : (29 × 13) = 200 : 377.

Given 377 units = ₹43,355 ⇒ 1 unit = 115.

Initial **Cost Price** for **A** = 200 × 115 = 23,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹23,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit of **A** = 45% | Profit of **B** = 30% | Final Price paid by **C** = ₹43,355

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/221307cb072b9c1d475a4cef8405c480ad467ce4c300b2e650e44874c4ed2c39.png] 

Let the **cost price** for **A** be x.

⇒ Price for **B** = x × (1 + 45/100) = 1.45x

⇒ Price for **C** = (1.45x) × (1 + 30/100) = 1.45x × 1.3

⇒ 1.885x = 43,355

⇒ x = 43,355 ÷ 1.885

⇒ x = 23,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹23,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Formula

When two profits x% and y% occur successively, the net profit percentage is given by [x + y + (x × y)/100]%.

Ratio Method for Profit/Loss

Profit of P% means CP : SP = 100 : (100 + P). This can be simplified into fractions for faster calculations in chains.

Cost Price (CP) vs Selling Price (SP)

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100. To find CP from SP, use CP = SP × 100 / (100 + Profit%).

questions.question: The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder of height 14 cm, is 88 cm². Find the total surface area of the cylinder.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder of height 14 cm, is 88 cm².

**Formula used:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cylinder = 2πrh

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a cylinder = 2πrh + 2πr²

**Calculation:**

Given CSA = 88 cm²

Height (h) = 14 cm

Using CSA formula:

2πrh = 88

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r × 14 = 88

⇒ 2 × 22 × r × 2 = 88

⇒ 88r = 88

⇒ r = 1 cm

Now, using TSA formula:

TSA = 2πrh + 2πr²

⇒ TSA = 2 × (22/7) × 1 × 14 + 2 × (22/7) × 1²

⇒ TSA = 2 × 22 × 2 + 2 × (22/7)

⇒ TSA = 88 + (44/7)

⇒ TSA = 88 + 6.2857

⇒ TSA = 94.2857

⇒ TSA = (660/7) cm²

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: In a right-angled triangle ABC such that ∠BAC = 90° and AD is perpendicular to BC. If the area of ΔABC is 63 cm², area of ΔACD = 7 cm², and AC = 5 cm, then the length of BC is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Area of ΔABC = 63 cm²

Area of ΔACD = 7 cm²

AC = 5 cm

**Formula used:**

If ΔABC ∼ ΔXYZ, then

ar(ΔABC) / ar(ΔXYZ) = (AB/XY)² = (BC/YZ)2 = (AC/XZ)2

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eb956877f6a76bd78a2be16fedfb79b974615ef705dee8dad8fe9661bd687061.png] 

In ΔABC and ΔACD

∠BAC = ∠ADC = 90° 

∠C = ∠C (Common in both triangles)

So, ΔABC ∼ ΔDAC (by AA Similarity)

Now,

ar(ΔABC) / ar(ΔACD) = (BC/AC)²

⇒ 63/7 = (BC/5)²

⇒ 9/1 = (BC/5)2

⇒ √(9/1) = BC/5

⇒ 3 = BC/5

⇒ BC = 5 × 3 = 15 cm

**∴ The length of BC is 15 cm**

questions.question: By selling an article at 66% of its marked price, a merchant makes a profit of 10%. If he sells the article at 80% of its marked price, then the profit percentage will be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate **Selling Price (SP)** in terms of **Cost Price (CP)** and **Marked Price (MP)**:

66% of **MP** = 110% of **CP** (since 10% profit is made)

⇒ 1% of **MP** = (110 / 66)% of **CP** = (5 / 3)% of **CP**

⇒ 80% of **MP** = (5 / 3) × 80% of **CP** = (400 / 3)% of **CP** = 133 1/3% of **CP**

⇒ **New Profit %** = 133 1/3% − 100% = 33 1/3%

**∴ The correct answer is 33 (1)/(3) %.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **SP₁** = 66% of **MP**, **Profit** = 10%, **SP₂** = 80% of **MP**.

**Formula:** **Cost Price (CP)** = [**Selling Price (SP)** / (100 + **Profit %**)] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dedd7bf725915491978f4dd710fffc958e112622e7f63c88bdf6248051755aaa.png] 

⇒ Let **Marked Price (MP)** = ₹100

⇒ Case 1: **SP₁** = 66% of 100 = ₹66

⇒ **CP** = (66 ÷ 110) × 100 = ₹60

⇒ Case 2: **SP₂** = 80% of 100 = ₹80

⇒ **Profit** = **SP₂** − **CP** = 80 − 60 = ₹20

⇒ **Profit %** = (20 ÷ 60) × 100 = (1/3) × 100

⇒ **Profit %** = 33 1/3%

**∴ The correct answer is 33 (1)/(3) %.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CP and MP Relationship

The ratio of **Marked Price** to **Cost Price** is given by: MP/CP = (100 + Profit %)/(100 − Discount %).

Profit and Loss Basics

**Profit %** = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100, and **Discount %** = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100. **Profit** or **Loss** is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless stated otherwise.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the **Equivalent Discount** is [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100]%.

Which course had the highest growth rate (in percentage) during the period from 2015 to 2020?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Enrollment data from 2015 to 2020 for different courses (Engineering, Science, Arts, Management)

**Formula used:**

Growth Rate (%) = [(Final Value - Initial Value) / Initial Value] × 100

**Calculation:**

For Engineering:

Initial Value (2015) = 1200, Final Value (2020) = 1400

Growth Rate = [(1400 - 1200) / 1200] × 100

⇒ Growth Rate = [200 / 1200] × 100

⇒ Growth Rate ≈ 16.67%

For Science:

Initial Value (2015) = 850, Final Value (2020) = 950

Growth Rate = [(950 - 850) / 850] × 100

⇒ Growth Rate = [100 / 850] × 100

⇒ Growth Rate ≈ 11.76%

For Arts:

Initial Value (2015) = 450, Final Value (2020) = 750

Growth Rate = [(750 - 450) / 450] × 100

⇒ Growth Rate = [300 / 450] × 100

⇒ Growth Rate ≈ 66.67%

For Management:

Initial Value (2015) = 240, Final Value (2020) = 320

Growth Rate = [(320 - 240) / 240] × 100

⇒ Growth Rate = [80 / 240] × 100

⇒ Growth Rate ≈ 33.33%

**∴ The course with the highest growth rate is Arts, with a growth rate of approximately 66.67%.**

questions.question: 18 men can complete (1)/(5) of a work in 10 days. How many people are required to complete (2)/(5) of the same work in 5 days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the MDH formula: (M₁ × D₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂) / W₂

Given: (18 × 10) / (1/5) = (M₂ × 5) / (2/5)

⇒ 180 × 5 = M₂ × 5 × (5/2)

⇒ 180 = M₂ × (5/2)

⇒ M₂ = (180 × 2) / 5 = 72

**∴ The correct option is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial men (M₁) = 18

Initial days (D₁) = 10

Initial work (W₁) = 1/5

New days (D₂) = 5

New work (W₂) = 2/5

**Formula Used:**

(M₁ × D₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂) / W₂

 CASE 1 Men (M1) = 18 Days (D1) = 10 Work (W1) = 1/5 CASE 2 Men (M2) = ? Days (D2) = 5 Work (W2) = 2/5 
• M1 × D1 / W1 = M2 × D2 / W2 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (18 × 10) / (1/5) = (M₂ × 5) / (2/5)

⇒ 180 × 5 = (M₂ × 5 × 5) / 2

⇒ 900 = (25 × M₂) / 2

⇒ 1800 = 25 × M₂

⇒ M₂ = 1800 / 25

⇒ M₂ = 72

**∴ The correct option is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

MDH Rule / Chain Rule

The general formula is (M₁ × D₁ × H₁ × E₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂ × E₂) / W₂, where M is men, D is days, H is hours, E is efficiency, and W is work.

Inverse Proportion

For a constant amount of work, the number of men is inversely proportional to the number of days taken: M₁D₁ = M₂D₂.

Work and Efficiency

Total work is the product of the number of workers, the time they work, and their individual efficiency: W = M × D × H × E.

questions.question: Two circles touch each other externally at M. PQ is a direct common tangent to the two circles, P and Q are points of contact and ∠MPQ = 38°. ∠MQP is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two **circles touching externally** at point **M**, the angle subtended by the **direct common tangent** **PQ** at the point of contact **M** is always **90°**.

⇒ ∠PMQ = 90°

In triangle **ΔPMQ**, the sum of angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠MQP = 90° − ∠MPQ

⇒ ∠MQP = 90° − 38° = 52°

**∴ The correct answer is 52°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

∠MPQ = 38°

Circles touch at **M**; **PQ** is a **direct common tangent**.

**Formula Used:**

1. Lengths of **tangents** from an **external point** to a circle are equal.

2. Sum of angles in a **triangle** = 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/febc15d212984e249bcc484d1872cd11280bba803157078fdea6ea0fd48cf688.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **common tangent** at **M** intersect **PQ** at point **R**.

⇒ From point **R**, **RP** and **RM** are tangents to the first circle, so **RP = RM**.

⇒ From point **R**, **RQ** and **RM** are tangents to the second circle, so **RQ = RM**.

⇒ Thus, **RP = RQ = RM**. This implies **R** is the midpoint of **PQ** and **RM = ½ PQ**.

⇒ In **ΔPMQ**, if the median **RM** is half the side **PQ**, then **∠PMQ = 90°**.

⇒ In **ΔPMQ**, ∠MPQ + ∠MQP + ∠PMQ = 180°

⇒ 38° + ∠MQP + 90° = 180°

⇒ ∠MQP = 180° − 128°

⇒ ∠MQP = 52°

**∴ The correct answer is 52°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

The length of the direct common tangent for two circles with radii r₁ and r₂ and distance d between centers is √(d² − (r₁ − r₂)²).

Tangents from an External Point

Tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are always equal in length and subtend equal angles at the center.

Circles Touching Externally

When two circles touch externally, the distance between their centers d = r₁ + r₂, and they have three common tangents (two direct and one transverse).</p

questions.question: What is the area of the region created by the two linear equations 2x + y = 6 and 2x - y = -2 bounded by these lines and the x-axis?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify the vertices of the triangle formed by the lines and the **x-axis** (where y = 0).

Line 1 (2x + y = 6) intersects x-axis at (3, 0) and Line 2 (2x − y = −2) intersects x-axis at (−1, 0).

The **base** of the triangle along the x-axis is |3 − (−1)| = 4 units.

Solve the equations for the intersection point: Adding 2x + y = 6 and 2x − y = −2 gives 4x = 4 ⇒ x = 1. Substitute x = 1 in 2x + y = 6 ⇒ 2(1) + y = 6 ⇒ y = 4.

The **height** of the triangle is the y-coordinate of the intersection point, which is 4 units.

Area = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 4 × 4 = 8 sq. units.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 sq. units.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given Equations:**

Equation 1: 2x + y = 6

Equation 2: 2x − y = −2

**Formula Used:**

Area of a triangle with base (b) and height (h) = 1/2 × b × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d0dc50e94951e1cc4142a116895cb52023c07be596cba1ac54dc8c336c31c35c.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculations:**

⇒ Finding x-intercept of 2x + y = 6: Set y = 0 ⇒ 2x = 6 ⇒ x = 3. Point A is (3, 0).

⇒ Finding x-intercept of 2x − y = −2: Set y = 0 ⇒ 2x = −2 ⇒ x = −1. Point C is (−1, 0).

⇒ Solving for intersection point P: Adding (2x + y) and (2x − y) = 6 + (−2) ⇒ 4x = 4 ⇒ x = 1.

⇒ Substituting x = 1 into 2x + y = 6 ⇒ 2(1) + y = 6 ⇒ y = 4. Point P is (1, 4).

⇒ Base of triangle along x-axis = xA − xC = 3 − (−1) = 4 units.

⇒ Height of triangle = y-coordinate of P = 4 units.

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 4 × 4 = 8 sq. units.

Therefore, the calculation shows the area of the region is 8 sq. units, which matches **Option (2)**.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 sq. units.**

**__Additional Information__**

Area of Triangle (Coordinate Geometry)

For vertices (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂), and (x₃, y₃), Area = 1/2 |x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|.

Intercept Form of Linear Equation

A line can be represented as x/a + y/b = 1, where 'a' is the x-intercept and 'b' is the y-intercept.

Region Bounded by Axes

If a region is bounded by the y-axis, use the x-coordinate of the intersection as the height and the difference between y-intercepts as the base.</p

questions.question: If a ∶ b = 3 ∶ 7 and b ∶ c = 4 ∶ 9, then find a ∶ b ∶ c.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

If a ∶ b = 3 ∶ 7 and b ∶ c = 4 ∶ 9

**Formula used:**

To find a ∶ b ∶ c, we need to make the values of b in both ratios equal.

**Calculation:**

a ∶ b = 3 ∶ 7

b ∶ c = 4 ∶ 9

Make the value of b equal in both ratios:

LCM of 7 and 4 = 28

Convert a ∶ b to have b = 28:

3 ∶ 7 = 3×4 ∶ 7×4 = 12 ∶ 28

Convert b ∶ c to have b = 28:

4 ∶ 9 = 4×7 ∶ 9×7 = 28 ∶ 63

Combine to get a ∶ b ∶ c:

12 ∶ 28 ∶ 63

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: Find the remainder when 179 × 172 × 173 is divided by 17.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Find the remainder when 179 × 172 × 173 is divided by 17.

**Formula used:**

Using the property of modular arithmetic:

(a × b) mod m = [(a mod m) × (b mod m)] mod m

**Calculation:**

179 mod 17 = 179 - (17 × 10) = 179 - 170 = 9

172 mod 17 = 172 - (17 × 10) = 172 - 170 = 2

173 mod 17 = 173 - (17 × 10) = 173 - 170 = 3

⇒ 179 × 172 × 173 mod 17 = (9 × 2 × 3) mod 17

⇒ 54 mod 17 = 54 - (17 × 3) = 54 - 51 = 3

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: The area of a rectangular field is 3600 m². If the field is 45 m long, what is its perimeter?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Width of the **rectangular field** = Area ÷ Length = 3600 ÷ 45 = 80 m.

**Perimeter** = 2 × (Length + Width) = 2 × (45 + 80) = 2 × 125 = 250 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 250 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Area** of the rectangle = 3600 m²

**Length** (L) of the rectangle = 45 m

**Formula Used:**

1. Area = Length × Width (W)

2. Perimeter = 2 × (Length + Width)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e0470a0a5c9057f2b35a1e94a5a784fe58f184a75c34984c3ad48a8108579a4d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = L × W

⇒ 3600 = 45 × W

⇒ W = 3600 ÷ 45

⇒ W = 80 m

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × (L + W)

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × (45 + 80)

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × 125

⇒ Perimeter = 250 m

Therefore, **Option 4** is the correct choice.

**∴ The correct answer is 250 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rectangle

A **rectangle** is a quadrilateral with four right angles. Opposite sides are equal and parallel. The diagonals bisect each other and are equal in length.

Important Formulas

1. **Diagonal (d)** = √(L² + W²)

2. If perimeter is P and length is L, then **Width** = (P ÷ 2) − L

3. A **square** is a special case of a rectangle where Length = Width.</p

questions.question: A person wants to buy 10 chairs. The total cost of 10 chairs is ₹4,500. After bargaining, the shopkeeper agrees to decrease the cost of each chair by 20%. Then the person purchased 10% more chairs. What will be the cost of the chairs that he purchased?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A person wants to buy 10 chairs. The total cost of 10 chairs is ₹4,500. After bargaining, the shopkeeper agrees to decrease the cost of each chair by 20%. Then the person purchased 10% more chairs.

**Formula used:**

New Cost of Each Chair = Original Cost of Each Chair × (1 - Discount Percentage)

Total Cost = Number of Chairs × New Cost of Each Chair

**Calculation:**

Original Cost of Each Chair = ₹4500 / 10

⇒ Original Cost of Each Chair = ₹450

New Cost of Each Chair = ₹450 × (1 - 0.20)

⇒ New Cost of Each Chair = ₹450 × 0.80

⇒ New Cost of Each Chair = ₹360

Number of Chairs Purchased = 10 + (10 × 0.10)

⇒ Number of Chairs Purchased = 10 + 1

⇒ Number of Chairs Purchased = 11

Total Cost = 11 × ₹360

⇒ Total Cost = ₹3960

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: A circle of diameter 26 cm has two equal parallel chords of length 10 cm each, then the distance between the two chords is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A circle of diameter 26 cm has two equal parallel chords of length 10 cm each.

**Formula used:**

Let the radius of the circle be R, and the distance of each chord from the center be d₁ and d₂.

Using the perpendicular distance formula from the center to a chord:

sqrt{R² - ((chord length)/(2))²} = distance from center to chord

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e68640bdb1ba9e1a76514957b0b28792fb7d9da9e16d86c0d7337c507d8ce92.png] 

Radius (R) = (26)/(2) = 13 cm

Half of chord length = (10)/(2) = 5 cm

Distance from center to each chord (d₁ and d₂):

sqrt{13² - 5²}

⇒ sqrt{169 - 25}

⇒ sqrt{144}

⇒ 12 cm

The distance between the two chords = 2 × 12 = 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: The salaries of T in twelve months of a year are: ₹12,000, ₹12,000, ₹12,000, ₹15,000, ₹15,000, ₹15,000, ₹21,000, ₹21,000, ₹21,000, ₹30,000, ₹30,000, ₹30,000. The average salary of T per month in ₹ is _______.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Since each **salary slab** occurs for the same duration (3 months each), the overall **average** is the simple average of the distinct salary values.

Average = (12000 + 15000 + 21000 + 30000) ÷ 4

Average = 78000 ÷ 4 = 19500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹19500.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Monthly salaries for 12 months in groups of 3 months each.

**Formula Used:** Average = Total Sum of Salaries ÷ Total Number of Months

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d2804715be65488cec66adc66dcd6f8f65f47924ffff8765df67ec7d3ebd4648.png] 

⇒ Total salary for first 3 months = 3 × 12000 = ₹36,000

⇒ Total salary for next 3 months = 3 × 15000 = ₹45,000

⇒ Total salary for next 3 months = 3 × 21000 = ₹63,000

⇒ Total salary for last 3 months = 3 × 30000 = ₹90,000

⇒ Sum of all salaries = 36000 + 45000 + 63000 + 90000 = ₹2,34,000

⇒ Average salary = 234000 ÷ 12

⇒ Average salary = ₹19500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹19500.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

The simple average of n observations is calculated as (x₁ + x₂ + ... + xₙ) ÷ n.

Weighted Average

When values have different weights/frequencies, Average = (Σwᵢxᵢ) ÷ (Σwᵢ), where w is the weight (frequency).

Average of Groups

If every group has the exact same number of items, the overall average is simply the average of the individual group averages.

questions.question: A policeman starts chasing a thief who is 500 m ahead of him. The speed of the thief is 18 km/h, and the speed of the policeman is 36 km/h. Find the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A policeman starts chasing a thief who is 500 m ahead of him. The speed of the thief is 18 km/h, and the speed of the policeman is 36 km/h.

**Formula used:**

Relative speed = Speed of policeman - Speed of thief

Time = Distance / Relative speed

**Calculations:**

Speed of thief = 18 km/h = 18 × (1000/3600) m/s = 5 m/s

Speed of policeman = 36 km/h = 36 × (1000/3600) m/s = 10 m/s

Relative speed = 10 m/s - 5 m/s = 5 m/s

Distance = 500 m

⇒ Time = 500 / 5

⇒ Time = 100 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: A fraction (3)/(5)is decreased by (2)/(5). The resulting fraction is then increased by 20%. What is the percentage decrease/increase in the value of the original fraction?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A fraction dfrac{3}{5} is decreased by dfrac{2}{5}. The resulting fraction is then increased by 20%.

**Formula used:**

New Value = Original Value × (1 + Percentage Change)

**Calculation:**

Initial Fraction = dfrac{3}{5}

Decreased Fraction: dfrac{3}{5} - dfrac{2}{5} = dfrac{1}{5}

Increased by 20%: dfrac{1}{5} times (1 + 0.20) = dfrac{1}{5} times 1.20

⇒ dfrac{1}{5} times 1.20 = dfrac{1.20}{5} = dfrac{6}{25}

Percentage Change = dfrac{dfrac{6}{25} - dfrac{3}{5}}{dfrac{3}{5}} times 100\%

⇒ dfrac{dfrac{6}{25} - dfrac{15}{25}}{dfrac{3}{5}} times 100\%

⇒ dfrac{-9}{25} times dfrac{5}{3} times 100 %

⇒ -60\%

**∴ The correct answer is option 3 i.e. decrease by 60%.**

questions.question: If the surface area of cuboid is 108 m², then find the height of the cuboid, whose length is 6 m and breadth is 3 m.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Surface area of cuboid (S) = 108 m²

Length (l) = 6 m

Breadth (b) = 3 m

**Formula used:**

S = 2(lb + bh + hl)

Where, h = height

**Calculation:**

108 = 2(6 × 3 + 3 × h + 6 × h)

⇒ 108 = 2(18 + 3h + 6h)

⇒ 108 = 2(18 + 9h)

⇒ 108 = 36 + 18h

⇒ 108 - 36 = 18h

⇒ 72 = 18h

⇒ h = 72 ÷ 18

⇒ h = 4 m

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**
